title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, timeouts
author: Ava Rodriguez
description: Context: continuous batching scheduler has been the primary mechanism for improving GPU utilization at low latency, but recent production signals showed unfair queueing across tenants, occasional starvation for small low-latency requests, and p99 timeouts under specific sequence-length distributions. Motivation: improve fairness across routes and customers, prevent starvation of short requests during heavy batching, tighten timeouts to avoid head-of-line blocking, and add observability + benchmarks to validate gains. Changes: 1) Scheduler queueing: introduce a hierarchical request queue with per-route token buckets and an adaptive admission window based on recent service time percentiles; this reduces long-tail queue growth for noisy routes. 2) Fairness: add a weighted deficit-round-robin pass to ensure proportional service across route weights while preserving batching opportunities; weights are configurable per-route and default to historical request share. 3) Starvation prevention: implement an age-based priority bump where requests exceeding a configurable starvation_threshold_ms are promoted to a fast-path queue with bounded batch size to guarantee latency SLOs for short requests. 4) Timeouts: add two-phase timeouts: a soft enqueue_timeout that triggers early partial-batch dispatch and a strict execution_timeout enforced before kernel scheduling to avoid long head-of-line blocking. Both timeouts are adaptive and smoothed over a short telemetry window. 5) Observability: emit new metrics (scheduler.queue_depth_by_route, scheduler.age_histogram_ms, scheduler.preemptions, scheduler.partial_dispatches) and trace spans for queueing/dispatch decisions. 6) Feature flag + rollout: changes gated behind runtime feature_flag continuous_batcher_scheduler_v2 with gradual rollout to Dedicated clusters, Canary pool, then global. 7) Tests and benchmarks: end-to-end unit and integration tests added, microbench harness for synthetic sequence-length mixes and p99 latency measurement. Rollout plan: enable flag in canary for 48 hours, monitor scheduler.{preemptions,p99_latency} and per-route SLA, then enable on Dedicated with 10% capacity increase guardrails.
